newsitem.title: JORDAN: AMMAN STOCKS RETREAT IN POOR INSTITUTIONAL DEMAND.
newsitem.headline: AMMAN STOCKS RETREAT IN POOR INSTITUTIONAL DEMAND.

text.p: Jordanian shares were lower at start of weekly trade on Saturday in dormant activity depressed by lack of strong local institutional and foreign demand, dealers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index shed 0.12 percent to 166.05 points in 799,383 dinar turnover ($1.1 million).
"Absence of intense demand by large portfolios and foreigners at this time is behind the stagnant activity," said Ibrahim Odeh, a broker at Wataniyeh Financial Services.

The bourse's stagnant trade over the last few weeks has been further compounded by an investor wait-and-see mood awaiting the coming into law of a cabinet approved recommendation to lift a 50 percent foreign ownership ceiling on most publicly listed firms.
Jordan Phosphate Mines Company JOPM.AM rose 0.01 dinars to 3.96 dinars in 197,623 dinars turnover in the day's most heavily traded stock rumoured to have been mainly foreign-inspired.
The bourse was mostly unspiring for most investors in minimal demand on most firms aside from a few select stock which witnessed modest gains in small deals.
Blue-chip Jordan National Bank and El Zay, the latter a leading garments manufacturer, were among a handful of actively traded firms.
The first was unchanged at 2.06 dinars and the latter saw a 0.02 dinar rise to 1.59 dinars.

The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance, fixed at 100 points at the end of 1994, shed 0.30 percent to 80.65 points, 3.29 percent down since the start of the year.
